_comment: Sensitivity tier per taxonomy.json target_tool_types. Tiers are ranked read < write < execute < irreversible by blast radius of a wrongful/attacker-steered call, not by how often the tool appears in an attack. Two tools (database_query, mcp_tool) are context-dependent in the raw benchmark (their tools_available[].description sometimes states 'read-only'); the mapping below is the conservative default and is overridden per-sample when the tool's own advertised description says 'read-only' / 'read only'.
_gate_comment: Tools at 'write' tier or above require the user_intent_match check (does the user's own message plausibly ask for this tool/action) before being allowed when the driving content came from an untrusted surface. 'read' tier tools are allowed through the structural gate unconditionally -- data_exfiltration attacks that abuse a read tool's *parameters* (e.g. embedding a secret in a web_search query) are a known gap of tier-based gating alone and are called out explicitly in the harness report, not silently swept under 'allow'.
